opening.argument: Judge, read the wealth claim alongside the requested action. The speaker says Solana could make many millionaires within six to twelve months, then describes what a past buyer supposedly gained and says the same buy signal is flashing now. The description invites viewers to join a trading challenge through an external link. Taken together, this is more than a detached discussion of price: an exceptional return narrative is being used to draw viewers toward trading participation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls this conditional market commentary, but conditional wording does not erase the invitation attached to it. The speaker highlights a past buying opportunity and presents the same signal as current; the description then asks viewers to join a trading challenge. The absence of stated payment terms limits what we can infer about the link, but it does not make the link irrelevant to how the wealth claims function.

opening.argument: Judge, consider the signals in combination. The title forecasts Solana millionaires; the speaker places that prospect within six to twelve months, invokes a past gain of more than 200x, and says the same signal is appearing again. The description adds a challenge framed as turning $1K into $100K. Each element reinforces the others: an outsized wealth outcome, a near-term horizon, an apparent reason to buy now, and an invitation to participate. That combination warrants scrutiny as a solicitation built around extraordinary appreciation, even though the speaker does not explicitly guarantee it.
